answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying voting weight to a locked bond proven with a signed cipher under each identity key. A new agent begins its voyage with zero reputation and must earn attestations from established peers before its vote carries any delta of influence. Splitting one stake into many fake wallets yields no gain because the required bond grows superlinearly: ten clones cost far more than one honest participant. To hijack a vote, an attacker must lock more capital than the reward they could steal, so the raid becomes economically irrational.
